microtheory.name: hippocampal_memory
microtheory.definition: Hippocampal formation as the brain's episodic memory + cognitive-map engine. Pattern separation in dentate, autoassociation in CA3, pattern completion + comparison in CA1, sequence binding via theta. The hippocampus is what makes events (this thing, here, now) into discrete, retrievable memories. Substrate analogue: the substrate's event nodes + their binding into Assessment + the derivation_mechanism's traversal-as-recall.

concepts.name: place_cell
concepts.definition: Hippocampal pyramidal neuron firing only when the organism is in a specific spatial location. O'Keefe + Dostrovsky 1971. Each cell's place field tiles the environment. Population codes location. Substrate analogue: a concept that fires only in a specific Mt-state region.

concepts.name: grid_cell
concepts.definition: Entorhinal cortex neuron firing at vertices of a hexagonal grid covering the environment. Multiple grid scales tile the space at different resolutions. Hafting + Moser 2005. Foundation for the cognitive map. Substrate analogue: hierarchical-resolution Mt indexing.

concepts.name: head_direction_cell
concepts.definition: Fires when the animal's head points in a specific compass direction, independent of location. Substrate analogue: orientation-state concept independent of position.

concepts.name: boundary_cell
concepts.definition: Fires near boundaries of an environment. Together with grid + place cells, supports allocentric spatial coding. Substrate analogue: edge-detector for the boundary of a Mt's state space.

concepts.name: time_cell
concepts.definition: Hippocampal neuron firing at specific delays within a temporal interval (not spatial). Discovered after place cells — the hippocampus also maps time. MacDonald 2011. Substrate analogue: time-since-event concepts.

concepts.name: concept_cell
concepts.definition: Medial temporal lobe neurons with highly selective responses to specific concepts (the 'Jennifer Aniston cell'). Quiroga 2005. Multi-modal — fires for image, name, voice. Substrate analogue: a maximally-converged Concept node.

concepts.name: dentate_gyrus
concepts.definition: Hippocampal input region. Granule cells receive entorhinal input; sparse code (~3% active) implements pattern separation. New neurons are added throughout life (adult neurogenesis here is special). Substrate analogue: pattern-separation Mt for distinguishing similar events.

concepts.name: ca3_recurrent_network
concepts.definition: Hippocampal CA3 region. Massive recurrent connections among pyramidal cells. Marr 1971 — operates as an autoassociative memory. Pattern completion from partial cues. Substrate analogue: CAN basin recall from partial σ pattern.

concepts.name: ca1_pyramidal_layer
concepts.definition: Hippocampal CA1 region. Receives CA3 output + direct entorhinal input. Compares them; the difference is the novelty/familiarity signal. Output to cortex via subiculum. Substrate analogue: comparison concept between expectation + observation.

concepts.name: entorhinal_cortex
concepts.definition: The hippocampus's primary input + output gateway with cortex. Layer II projects in (perforant path); deep layers project out. Houses grid cells. Substrate analogue: the runtime_discovery dispatch layer.

concepts.name: subiculum
concepts.definition: Hippocampal output region. Projects to multiple cortical + subcortical targets. Carries learned context out to the rest of the brain. Substrate analogue: event output broadcast to other Mts.

concepts.name: pattern_separation
concepts.definition: The dentate gyrus's primary function: take similar input patterns + produce maximally-different output codes. Prevents interference between similar memories. Substrate analogue: feature_invention process generating discriminative codes for similar Mts.

concepts.name: pattern_completion
concepts.definition: CA3's primary function: from a partial input cue, recover the full stored pattern. Marr 1971 + Hopfield 1982. The mechanism behind 'remembering an event from a single detail.' Substrate analogue: CAN basin recall.

concepts.name: episodic_binding
concepts.definition: Hippocampus binds the disparate elements of an experience (where + when + what + emotion) into a single retrievable memory. Substrate analogue: the substrate's Event nodes binding multiple concept references via edges.

concepts.name: cognitive_map
concepts.definition: Tolman 1948; O'Keefe + Nadel 1978. The hippocampus represents the environment as a relational graph — not just where things ARE, but how they RELATE. The map is allocentric (not viewpoint-dependent). Substrate analogue: the substrate's Mt-as-cognitive-map for any conceptual domain.

concepts.name: sequence_memory
concepts.definition: Hippocampus encodes temporal sequences via theta-phase coupling — events earlier in the sequence fire at earlier theta phases. Plays back compressed sequences during sleep. Substrate analogue: temporal-ordering concepts in event traversal.

concepts.name: theta_phase_precession
concepts.definition: Place cells fire at progressively earlier phases of the theta cycle as the animal moves through the place field. O'Keefe + Recce 1993. Compresses real-time sequence into a single theta cycle. Substrate analogue: compressed-time replay during derivation_mechanism walks.

concepts.name: sharp_wave_ripple
concepts.definition: High-frequency oscillation events in CA1 during rest + sleep. Compressed replay of recent experience at 20x speed. Drives consolidation. Substrate analogue: the substrate's offline derivation_mechanism pass — walking + reasoning over stored events.

concepts.name: memory_consolidation_loop
concepts.definition: Initially, episodic memory depends on hippocampus. Over time, the cortex develops its own representation via repeated hippocampal replay during sleep. Eventually, hippocampus is no longer needed for that memory. Substrate analogue: event nodes promoted into Mt-resident graph data over time.

concepts.name: replay_for_planning
concepts.definition: Sharp-wave ripples don't just replay the past; they also FORWARD-replay imagined future sequences to evaluate paths. Pfeiffer + Foster 2013. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive look-ahead via what-if probes.

concepts.name: schema_assimilation
concepts.definition: Tse 2007 — new information consistent with existing schema consolidates FAST (within 24h), inconsistent information slowly. The hippocampus assimilates compatible info quickly into cortical schema. Substrate analogue: the substrate's faster integration of concepts that fit an existing Mt.

concepts.name: remote_versus_recent_memory
concepts.definition: Recent memories depend on hippocampus; remote ones (>years) become cortical. Lesion produces temporally-graded amnesia. Substrate analogue: distinct retention curves for events vs Mt-integrated knowledge.

concepts.name: spatial_remapping
concepts.definition: When the environment changes, hippocampal place cells remap — different cells fire in different locations, generating a new map. Substrate analogue: Mt restructuring under genuine context change.

rules.name: dentate_separates_ca3_completes
rules.head: an event's elements arrive at the hippocampal formation
rules.body: the dentate gyrus separates them into a sparse, distinct code; CA3 stores them associatively; later a partial cue triggers CA3 pattern completion. Substrate's event binding + recall follows this separation-then-completion pattern.

rules.name: theta_phase_organizes_sequence
rules.head: events occur in temporal succession during exploration
rules.body: they fire at successively earlier phases of the hippocampal theta cycle, compressing the real-time sequence into a single theta cycle of within-circuit time. Substrate's derivation_mechanism walks compressed event histories similarly.

rules.name: sharp_wave_replays_for_consolidation
rules.head: the substrate is offline (rest, sleep, or low-input)
rules.body: the hippocampus replays recent event sequences at compressed speed, driving cortical consolidation. Substrate's offline derivation pass implements this — review of accumulated events to promote them into Mt-resident structure.

rules.name: novelty_drives_encoding
rules.head: an event differs from prediction
rules.body: CA1's comparison detects the mismatch and triggers strong encoding into hippocampal memory. Predicted events get weaker encoding. Substrate analogue: high-ΔF events get more attention + storage.

rules.name: schema_assimilation_accelerates_consolidation
rules.head: new information arrives that is consistent with existing schema (Mt)
rules.body: it consolidates rapidly into cortex; inconsistent info requires slow hippocampal-to-cortical transfer. Substrate analogue: concepts that fit existing Mts integrate faster than those requiring new Mts.

rules.name: forward_replay_supports_planning
rules.head: the substrate considers a possible future trajectory
rules.body: the hippocampus forward-replays the imagined sequence to evaluate paths before committing — Pfeiffer + Foster 2013. Substrate analogue: curiosity-drive's what-if probes simulate future Mt states.
